newsitem.title: USA: Natl Fuel, Tenneco plan offshore pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Natl Fuel, Tenneco plan offshore pipeline.

text.p: National Fuel Gas Supply Corp said it and Tenneco Energy will form a 50-50 partnership to develop the $200 million Green Canyon Gathering System Tenneco proposed for the Gulf of Mexico.

In June, the Tenneco Inc subsidiary asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to rule that the project falls outside of its jurisdiction. A FERC ruling is expected shortly, the National Fuel Gas Co subsidiary said.

It said the partnership will build, own and operate a 24-inch, 153-mile offshore pipeline to gather and transport natural gas from the Green Canyon, Ewing Bank, Mississippi Canyon, Ship Shoal, Grand Isle and South Timbalier areas.
The two companies will also build a natural gas processing plant at the terminal end of the pipeline in Lafourche Parish, La., that can process 300 million cubic feet of gas per day.

With capacity of approximately 515 MMcf/d, the pipeline will be able to access 3.4 trillion cubic feet of estimated Outer Continental Shelf reserves and will provide access to five onshore pipelines in South Louisiana.
The companies are studying project financing of the pipeline, spokeswomen for both said.

"National Fuel has long desired to expand into the gathering and processing business," chief executive Bernard J. Kennedy said. "The Green Canyon Project represents a natural extension for us into a new area of our industry."
